step1_summary: Symptom details: • Onset ~5 days ago, began over the weekend • Dry, hacking cough • Runny nose • Myalgias, chills, occasional headache • No sputum, no hemoptysis • No shortness of breath, wheeze, or chest tightness • No palpable neck glands reported
Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (≈5–6 yrs); mild hypertension
Medications: Metformin; Lisinopril; intermittently using paracetamol for current symptoms. No ibuprofen taken.  Allergies: none mentioned
Family/social history: not discussed (secure location confirmed). No smoking/alcohol data provided.

Vital signs / exam: Home BP “within normal range” this morning; no other vitals given. Video exam—mild pharyngeal erythema, no tonsillar hypertrophy or exudate, no cervical lymphadenopathy, chest not examined.

V: Pulmonary embolism: Can present with new-onset cough, but absence of dyspnea, pleuritic pain, or risk factors makes it less likely.
I: Viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold): Classic constellation of dry cough, rhinorrhea, myalgias, low-grade symptoms for <1 week.
Influenza / influenza-like illness: Systemic myalgias, chills, headache with cough could represent early influenza.
COVID-19 (if circulating): Dry cough, myalgias and mild URTI symptoms.
N: Early lung cancer: Can present with dry cough, but 5-day duration and acute viral features argue against.
D: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation: Would require smoking history and usually productive cough or dyspnea—unlikely here.
I2: ACE-inhibitor-induced cough (lisinopril): Classically dry, non-productive, can begin anytime after initiation.
C: Primary ciliary dyskinesia: Recurrent URTIs/cough since childhood—no such history.
A: Allergic rhinitis with post-nasal drip: Runny nose and cough without fever could fit.
T: Airway irritation from environmental exposure (dust, smoke): Not described.
E: Diabetic ketoacidosis: Can cause Kussmaul respiration, not mild dry cough; blood sugars reported stable.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold / rhinovirus, etc.)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Acute onset (<1 wk) of dry cough, rhinorrhea, mild pharyngeal erythema, myalgias, afebrile, self-limited course—classic for common cold.
Systemic symptoms (myalgias, chills, headache) with cough could represent early influenza, although severity appears mild and no fever reported.
Patient takes lisinopril; ACE-I cough is dry and non-productive. However onset is usually subacute/chronic and not associated with rhinorrhea or systemic symptoms.
Runny nose and cough without lower-respiratory findings could be allergic, but systemic aches/chills point more toward infectious etiology.

supporting_evidence: Dry cough plus rhinorrhea, pharyngeal erythema
No focal chest findings or shortness of breath
opposing_evidence: No specific mention of fever (common but not universal)

supporting_evidence: Cough with myalgias, chills, headache—classic influenza triad
opposing_evidence: No high fever, no severe fatigue
Onset only 5 days ago despite being on lisinopril long term
Concurrent rhinorrhea and systemic viral symptoms not typical for ACE-I cough

supporting_evidence: Mild pharyngeal erythema without tonsillar enlargement
opposing_evidence: Presence of systemic symptoms (myalgias, chills) favor infection
